key_insight: Euclid-MCP adds a standardized MCP layer over SWI-Prolog so LLMs can offload multi-step logical reasoning to a deterministic symbolic engine.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical, tool-augmented reasoning substrate for compliance and security workflows where correctness, traceability, and reproducibility matter.
method: Introduces Euclid-IR, a human-readable Horn-clause intermediate representation that LLMs can generate reliably.
Compiles Euclid-IR to Prolog or other backends and exposes a compact translate-run-inspect-repair tool loop.
Returns proof traces and derivation logs so clients can inspect and refine reasoning steps.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on an IT security and compliance use case: LLMs work on small knowledge bases, but hallucinate on larger ones, while Euclid-MCP produces exact answers with lower latency and more compact outputs.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the translated rules and backend integration, so malformed Euclid-IR or Prolog-specific constraints may limit portability or correctness.
paper_title: Euclid-MCP: A Model Context Protocol Server for Deterministic Logical Reasoning via Prolog
